summary: A korban that comes more often goes first. So the tamid comes before the mussaf, and the mussaf of Shabbos comes before the mussaf of Rosh Chodesh.

chunks.en: Anything that is more frequent than another
chunks.st: Any offering that is more frequent than another

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes the other offering. Therefore,

chunks.en: The tamid korbanos come before the mussaf korbanos,
chunks.st: the daily offerings precede the additional offerings,
chunks.stMore: which are sacrificed only on certain days. When Shabbat and the New Moon coincide,

words.note: The korbanos brought every morning and afternoon.
Extra korbanos brought on Shabbos and Yom Tov.

chunks.he: מוּסְפֵי שַׁבָּת קוֹדְמִין לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ,
chunks.en: the mussaf of Shabbos comes before the mussaf of Rosh Chodesh,
chunks.st: the additional Shabbat offerings precede the additional New Moon offerings. Likewise,

chunks.en: the mussaf of Rosh Chodesh comes before
chunks.st: the additional New Moon offerings precede

chunks.en: the mussaf of Rosh Hashanah,
chunks.st: the additional New Year offerings.
chunks.stMore: The mishna cites the source for the principle that the frequent precedes the less frequent:

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: As it is stated with regard to the additional offerings of the first day of Passover: “

chunks.en: "Besides the morning olah, which is for the olah
chunks.st: Besides the burnt offering of the morning, which is for a

chunks.en: of the tamid, you shall make these."
chunks.st: daily burnt offering, you shall offer these”
chunks.stMore: (Numbers 28:23). The verse indicates that the daily offering is sacrificed first, and then the additional offerings are sacrificed.

summary: A holier korban goes first. The mishnah lists the order: chatas, asham, todah and nazir's ram, shelamim, and bechor, and gives the reason for each one.

chunks.en: And anything that is holier than another
chunks.st: Any offering that is more sacred than another

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes the other
chunks.stMore: offering. The mishna elaborates: If there is blood of a sin offering and blood of a burnt offering to be presented,

chunks.en: The blood of a chatas comes before the blood of an olah,
chunks.st: the blood of the sin offering precedes the blood of the burnt offering

chunks.en: because it brings forgiveness.
chunks.st: because it effects acceptance,
chunks.stMore: i.e., atonement, for severe transgressions punishable by karet. Likewise, if there are limbs of a burnt offering and portions of a sin offering to be burned on the altar,

chunks.en: Parts of an olah come before the fats of a chatas,
chunks.st: the burning of the limbs of the burnt offering precedes the portions of the sin offering,

words.en: the parts for the mizbeach of

chunks.en: because they are all burned in the fire.
chunks.st: because the burnt offering is entirely burned in the flames
chunks.stMore: on the altar, whereas only part of the sin offering is burned. Similarly, although both effect atonement,

chunks.en: A chatas comes before an asham,
chunks.st: a sin offering precedes a guilt offering

chunks.en: because its blood is put on
chunks.st: due to the fact that its blood is placed on

chunks.en: the four corners and on the base.
chunks.st: the four corners of the altar and the remnants of its blood are poured on the base
chunks.stMore: of the altar, whereas the blood of the guilt offering is sprinkled on only two corners of the altar.

chunks.en: An asham comes before a todah and a nazir's ram,
chunks.st: A guilt offering precedes a thanks offering and the nazirite’s ram

chunks.en: because it is one of the holiest korbanos.
chunks.st: due to the fact that it is an offering of the most sacred order, and the others are offerings of lesser sanctity.

chunks.en: The todah and the nazir's ram come before shelamim,
chunks.st: A thanks offering and a nazirite’s ram precede a peace offering

chunks.en: because they are eaten for one day,
chunks.st: due to the fact that they are eaten for one day,
chunks.stMore: like offerings of the most sacred order, whereas a peace offering is eaten for two days,

chunks.en: and they need loaves of bread.
chunks.st: and the thanks offering and nazirite’s ram require loaves
chunks.stMore: to be brought with them, four types with the thanks offering and two types with the nazirite’s ram.

chunks.en: Shelamim come before a bechor,
chunks.st: Sacrifice of the peace offering precedes sacrifice of the firstborn

chunks.en: because they need four puttings of blood,
chunks.st: offering due to the fact that the peace offering requires placing the blood on the altar, in the form of two placements that are four,

chunks.en: and semichah, nesachim, and waving the chest and thigh.
chunks.st: and placing hands on the head of the offering, and libations, and the wavings of the breast and the thigh
chunks.stMore: by the priest and the owner; none of which is required for the firstborn offering.

words.note: Leaning with the hands on the korban's head.

summary: A bechor goes before maaser because it is holy from birth and eaten by Kohanim. Maaser goes before bird korbanos because it is shechted and has holiest parts, its blood and its fats.

chunks.he: הַבְּכוֹר קוֹדֵם לַמַּעֲשֵׂר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם,
chunks.en: The bechor comes before maaser because it is holy from birth,
chunks.st: The firstborn offering precedes the animal tithe offering because it is sanctified from the womb,
chunks.stMore: i.e., unlike the animal tithe offering it does not require consecration,

words.note: It is holy from the moment it is born.

chunks.en: and it is eaten by the Kohanim.
chunks.st: and it is eaten by the priests, whereas everyone may partake of the animal tithe offering.

chunks.en: Maaser comes before birds,
chunks.st: The animal tithe offering precedes bird

chunks.en: because it is a shechted korban and there are
chunks.st: offerings due to the fact that it requires slaughtering, whereas the bird’s nape is pinched; and there are

chunks.en: in it parts of the holiest korbanos:
chunks.st: two elements of the animal tithe offering that have the status of offerings of the most sacred order:

chunks.en: its blood and its fats.
chunks.st: Its blood that is presented on the altar and its portions
chunks.stMore: that are burned on the altar, whereas with regard to bird offerings only the blood is presented on the altar.

words.en: and its parts for the mizbeach

summary: Bird korbanos go before menachos because they have blood. A sinner's mincha goes before a mincha given as a gift, and a bird chatas goes before a bird olah.

chunks.en: Birds come before menachos,
chunks.st: The bird offerings precede meal offerings

chunks.en: because they are kinds with blood.
chunks.st: due to the fact that they are types whose blood is presented, and atonement is effected by the blood.

chunks.en: A sinner's mincha comes before a gift mincha,
chunks.st: The meal offering of a sinner precedes a voluntary meal offering

chunks.en: because it comes for a sin.
chunks.st: due to the fact that it comes to atone for a sin.

chunks.en: A bird chatas comes before a bird olah.
chunks.st: For the same reason the sacrifice of the bird sin offering precedes the sacrifice of the bird burnt offering,

chunks.en: And so too when setting it aside as holy.
chunks.st: and likewise with regard to its consecration, the sin offering takes precedence.

summary: Every chatas goes before every asham, except the asham of a metzora, which makes him ready to become tahor. Most asham korbanos are two-year-old rams worth two shekels, but those of a nazir and a metzora are one year old.

chunks.en: All the chatas korbanos in the Torah
chunks.st: All the sin offerings mandated by the Torah

chunks.en: come before the asham korbanos,
chunks.st: take precedence over the guilt offerings, as explained in the previous mishna (89a),

chunks.en: except for the asham of a metzora,
chunks.st: except for the guilt offering of a leper,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא בָא עַל יְדֵי הֶכְשֵׁר.
chunks.en: because it comes to make him fit.
chunks.st: because it comes to render one fit.
chunks.stMore: One who has been cured of leprosy must undergo a process through which he is rendered ritually pure before coming into contact with consecrated items. Although he must also bring a sin offering, his guilt offering is more central to that process of purification and therefore it takes precedence over the sin offering.

words.note: It helps make the metzora tahor again.

chunks.en: All the asham korbanos in the Torah come as
chunks.st: All the guilt offerings mandated by the Torah come

chunks.en: two years old and come worth silver shekels,
chunks.st: as rams in their second year, and come worth two silver shekels,

chunks.en: except for the asham of a nazir and the asham of a metzora,
chunks.st: except for the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper,

chunks.en: which come one year old
chunks.st: as they come from sheep in their first year,

chunks.en: and do not need to be worth silver shekels.
chunks.st: and do not need to come worth two silver shekels, as they have no fixed value.

summary: The holier korbanos are also eaten first. Rabbi Meir says yesterday's shelamim are eaten before today's chatas and asham; the Sages say the chatas goes first because it is one of the holiest korbanos.

chunks.en: Just as they come first in offering them,
chunks.st: Just as the more sacred offerings precede other offerings with regard to their sacrifice, as taught in the previous mishna (89a),

chunks.en: so they come first in eating them.
chunks.st: they also precede the others with regard to their consumption.

chunks.he: שְׁלָמִים שֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ וּשְׁלָמִים שֶׁל הַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: Shelamim from yesterday and shelamim from today,
chunks.st: If one has a peace offering from yesterday and a peace offering from today,

chunks.en: the ones from yesterday come first.
chunks.st: the peace offering from yesterday precedes the peace offering from today.

chunks.en: Shelamim from yesterday and a chatas
chunks.st: If one has a peace offering from yesterday and a sin offering

chunks.en: or an asham from today,
chunks.st: or a guilt offering from today,

chunks.en: the shelamim from yesterday come first,
chunks.st: the peace offering from yesterday precedes the others;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: the chatas comes first,
chunks.st: The sin offering precedes the peace offering,

chunks.en: because it is one of the holiest korbanos.
chunks.st: due to the fact that it is an offering of the most sacred order.
chunks.stMore: Likewise, the guilt offering precedes the peace offering, as it is also of the most sacred order.

summary: The Kohanim may eat korbanos cooked any way they like and add regular spices. Rabbi Shimon says they may also add terumah spices, but Rabbi Meir says not, so the terumah will not become pasul.

chunks.en: And with all of them, the Kohanim may change how they eat them,
chunks.st: And with regard to all of the offerings that are eaten, the priests are permitted to alter the manner of their consumption and eat them as they choose. Therefore,

chunks.en: to eat them roasted,
chunks.st: the priests are permitted to eat them roasted,

chunks.en: or boiled, or cooked,
chunks.st: or boiled, or cooked,

words.note: Cooked a long time until very soft.

chunks.he: וְלָתֵת לְתוֹכָן תִּבְלֵי חֻלִּין וְתִבְלֵי תְרוּמָה,
chunks.en: and to put into them regular spices or terumah spices,
chunks.st: and to place in the cooking pot non-sacred spices or teruma spices.

words.note: A gift of food for the Kohanim.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Shimon.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he should not put terumah spices into them,
chunks.st: One may not place teruma spices in it,

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה לִידֵי פְסוּל:
chunks.en: so that he does not bring the terumah to becoming pasul.
chunks.st: so that he will not bring the teruma to a state of disqualification.
chunks.stMore: Consumption of consecrated foods is permitted only for a limited period, after which they are disqualified and burned. Adding teruma spices might cause those spices to be similarly disqualified.

words.note: Leftover korban meat must be burned, and the terumah spices would have to be burned with it.

summary: Rabbi Shimon says that oil given out to the Kohanim, or oil burned on the mizbeach, comes from certain menachos or the metzora's oil, because people do not give oil as a gift. Rabbi Tarfon says people may give oil as a gift.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.he: אִם רָאִיתָ שֶׁמֶן שֶׁהוּא מִתְחַלֵּק בָּעֲזָרָה,
chunks.en: If you saw oil being shared out in the courtyard,
chunks.st: If you saw oil that is being distributed in the Temple courtyard
chunks.stMore: for consumption by the priests and you seek to ascertain its nature,

chunks.he: אֵין אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לִשְׁאוֹל מַה הוּא,
chunks.en: you do not need to ask what it is.
chunks.st: you do not need to ask what it is.

chunks.en: It is the leftover of the wafers of the menachos of Yisrael,
chunks.st: Rather, it is left over from the oil of the wafers of the meal offerings of Israelites after they smeared a bit of oil on them,

words.note: Menachos brought by people who are not Kohanim.

chunks.en: and the log of oil of a metzora.
chunks.st: or it is left over from the log of oil of a leper after a small amount of the oil was placed on him.

chunks.en: If you saw oil that is
chunks.st: If you saw oil that is

chunks.en: put on the fires,
chunks.st: placed on the flames of the altar in the manner of an offering,

chunks.he: אֵין אַתָּה צָרִיךְ לִשְׁאוֹל מַה הוּא,
chunks.en: you do not need to ask what it is.
chunks.st: you do not need to ask what it is.

chunks.en: It is the leftover of the wafers of the menachos of Kohanim,
chunks.st: Rather, it is left over from the oil of the wafers of the meal offering of priests,

chunks.en: and the mincha of the Kohen Gadol.
chunks.st: or it is the leftover oil from the meal offering of the anointed priest,
chunks.stMore: which requires a great deal of oil and which is burned in its entirety on the altar. The mishna adds: One can-not say that the oil distributed to priests or burned on the altar was brought as a gift offering,

chunks.en: Because people do not give oil as a gift.
chunks.st: as one may not contribute oil as a gift offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: people may give oil as a gift.
chunks.st: One may contribute oil as a gift offering.
